title: MRI brain-age estimates were higher in a cerebral-palsy cohort
summary: A CNN trained on healthy MRI was applied to a retrospective cohort of 455 children and young adults with cerebral palsy. Model-derived brain age exceeded that of the healthy comparison group (20.28 versus 0.25 years of BrainAGE; p<0.0001), and the paper reports sex and CP-subtype differences. BrainAGE is a model-derived proxy, and this cross-sectional single-center result has no independent CP replication or clinical-outcome validation.
ai_technology: Two-dimensional convolutional neural network for MRI brain-age estimation
organization: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

evidence.tested: The model’s healthy-data test MAE was 3.98 years (r=0.95); the CP analysis was cross-sectional and not independently replicated.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN generated brain-age estimates used to compare cerebral-palsy participants with healthy controls and examine subgroup differences.
